The audit itself

Four tests. Run like a real customer, not a checklist bot.

We don't scrape your site and mail you a grade. We do what your next customer does — search, click, call, submit — and we time everything.

Test 01Website form

Does your form actually reach a human?

We submit your contact / quote form with a real-looking request, then watch: Does it go through? Who gets notified? How fast does a reply come — and is it a reply a customer would act on?

We check: delivery, notification inbox, spam-folder traps, reply speed, reply quality, mobile form usability.

Test 02After-hours phone

What happens when someone calls at 6:42 PM?

We call your business number after hours and again on a weekend — the exact moment your best leads call. Voicemail with no follow-up is a leak. So is a full mailbox, or a number that just rings.

We check: answer path, voicemail greeting, text-back (if any), callback by next business morning.

Test 03Google listing

Can Google send you a customer cleanly?

We pull up your Google Business Profile the way a searcher sees it and verify every tap: call button, directions, hours, website link, messaging. One wrong digit quietly deletes customers for months.

We check: phone accuracy, hours, category, service area, review count & recency, photo freshness.

Test 04Follow-up

What happens after the first contact?

We track the full arc: if we don't reply to your reply, do you follow up? Once? Twice? Ever? Most businesses stop at one touch — and most sales need more than one.

We check: follow-up count and timing, quote reminders, how the lead is tracked (if anywhere).

Who this is for

Built for businesses that live on inbound leads.

If your next customer finds you on Google, calls a number, or fills out a form, this audit is about your money.

Contractors & trades

Roofing, remodeling, HVAC, plumbing, electrical. You're on a ladder or under a house when the phone rings — the audit shows what those missed moments cost and which ones a simple system can catch.

Law offices

Intake is your front door. A slow reply or a form that lands in the wrong inbox sends a stressed client straight to the next firm on the search results. We test intake the way a prospective client experiences it.

Home services

Landscaping, cleaning, pest control, garage doors, movers. High call volume, seasonal spikes, lots of "we'll get back to you" — exactly the conditions where leads quietly leak away.

Fair questions

Before you ask.

Is it really free? What's the catch?+

It's free, and the "catch" is transparent: the audit is how we meet businesses we can help. If your report shows leaks worth fixing and you'd like help, we'll offer the $200 pilot. If not — or if you fix them yourself — the report is still yours. No invoice follows you around.

Will the test call and form confuse my team?+

Briefly, maybe — it has to look like a real customer inquiry to test anything real. Both touches are identified clearly in your report (exact times and what we said), and there's exactly one of each per channel. Most owners tell us the moment of confusion was itself a finding.

What do you need from me?+

Your business name, your website, and the phone number customers call. That's it. We don't need logins, passwords, or access to anything — everything we test is what the public can already reach.

How long until I see the report?+

Three to five business days. The tests are deliberately spread out — an after-hours call has to happen after hours, and a fair follow-up test takes a few days of silence on our end.

I'm not a contractor or a lawyer. Still worth it?+

If customers find you online and reach out by phone or form, yes. The audit was built for local service businesses generally — the leaks just tend to be most expensive where one job is worth thousands, or one client is worth more.

What happens to my information?+

It goes in one email, from you to us, and it's used to run your audit and send your report. No mailing list, no selling data, no sharing your findings with anyone. Anonymized lessons ("a roofer's form went to a dead inbox") may become a public teardown post — never with your name or business attached unless you say yes.
